grammar.title: Possessive adjectives: mon, ma, mes…
explanation: Possessive adjectives mean 'my', 'your', 'his', 'her', 'our' and 'their'. They go before the noun: mon père (my father), ma mère (my mother).

In French, the possessive agrees with the thing you have, not with the person who has it. Père is masculine, so it is mon père. Mère is feminine, so it is ma mère. For plural nouns, use mes: mes parents, mes sœurs.
Son, sa and ses mean 'his' AND 'her'. The noun decides the form: sa mère can be 'his mother' or 'her mother'. Son père can be 'his father' or 'her father'.
Before a feminine noun that starts with a vowel or a silent h, use mon, ton, son (not ma, ta, sa). It is easier to say: mon amie (my female friend), ton école, son histoire.

For 'our', 'your' (vous) and 'their', there is one singular form for masculine and feminine: notre, votre, leur. The plural forms are nos, vos, leurs: notre fils, nos enfants, leur maison, leurs amis.
Tu or vous? Use ton, ta, tes with a friend or a child (tu). Use votre, vos with a person you don't know well, or with several people (vous).

examples.fr: Mon père est cuisinier et ma mère est avocate.
examples.en: My father is a cook and my mother is a lawyer.
My grandparents live in Quebec City.
Paul loves his sister very much.
Léa is talking with her father.

examples.fr: Tu as une photo de ta famille ?
examples.en: Do you have a photo of your family?

examples.fr: Monsieur et Madame Dubois, vos enfants sont très gentils.
examples.en: Mr and Mrs Dubois, your children are very kind.

examples.fr: Ils aiment leur fille et leurs petits-enfants.
examples.en: They love their daughter and their grandchildren.

commonMistakes.why: Amie starts with a vowel, so ma becomes mon, even though amie is feminine.
The form depends on the noun, not on Julie. Père is masculine, so it is son, even when it means 'her father'.
Enfants is plural, so leur takes an -s: leurs.
Parents is plural, so use mes.

grammar.title: Adjectives: agreement and position
explanation: In French, an adjective changes to match the noun: masculine or feminine, singular or plural. Un garçon blond, une fille blonde, des garçons blonds, des filles blondes.

To make the feminine, you usually add -e: grand → grande, français → française. If the adjective already ends in -e, nothing changes: jeune, mince, belge. Some adjectives change more: -ien → -ienne (canadien → canadienne), -eux → -euse (paresseux → paresseuse), -eur → -euse (travailleur → travailleuse).
A few common adjectives are irregular. Learn them by heart: beau → belle, vieux → vieille, gros → grosse, roux → rousse.
To make the plural, you usually add -s: grands, grandes. If the masculine already ends in -s or -x, nothing changes: français, vieux, gros. Beau becomes beaux.
Most adjectives go AFTER the noun: un homme intelligent, une femme canadienne, des cheveux blonds. Nationalities and colours always go after the noun.
A small group of short, very common adjectives go BEFORE the noun: beau, joli, petit, grand, jeune, vieux, bon. Une petite fille, un grand garçon, une jolie photo, un bon ami.

examples.fr: Mon frère est grand et ma sœur est grande aussi.
examples.en: My brother is tall and my sister is tall too.

examples.fr: Ma grand-mère est vieille, mais elle est belle.
examples.en: My grandmother is old, but she is beautiful.
She is a young Italian actress.

commonMistakes.why: Mère is feminine, so the adjective takes -e.
Most adjectives go after the noun. Intelligent is not in the short group (beau, petit, grand…).
Petit is one of the short adjectives that go before the noun.
Enfants is plural, so the adjective takes -s.
Vieux is irregular: the feminine is vieille.

exercises.explanation: Mère is feminine and starts with a consonant, so 'my' is ma. Mon is for masculine nouns, mes for plural nouns.
Amie is feminine but starts with a vowel, so sa becomes son. Ses is for plural nouns, and leur means 'their'.
Enfants is plural and there are several owners, so 'their' is leurs. Leur is for one thing; ses and son mean 'his' or 'her'.
Sœur is feminine and singular, so add -e: grande. Grand is masculine; grands and grandes are plural.
Nationalities go after the noun and agree with it: une femme canadienne. Canadien is masculine, and the feminine of -ien doubles the n: -ienne.

exercises.prompt: Marc works in a restaurant and brings the food to the tables. What is his job?
exercises.explanation: A serveur brings food and drinks in a restaurant. An avocat works in law, a coiffeur cuts hair and a policier works for the police.

exercises.translation: We love our grandparents very much.
exercises.explanation: Grands-parents is plural, so 'our' is nos. Notre is only for one thing.

exercises.translation: Do you live with your family?
exercises.explanation: With vous, 'your' is votre for one thing, masculine or feminine. Vos is for plural nouns.

exercises.prompt: Complete with italien in the correct form.
exercises.explanation: Cousines is feminine plural: italien → italienne (double n + e) → italiennes (+ s).

exercises.translation: My daughter is six years old.
exercises.explanation: In French you HAVE an age: elle a six ans. Don't use être for age.

exercises.prompt: Complete with beau in the correct form.
exercises.explanation: Beau is irregular: the feminine is belle. It goes before the noun, like petit and grand.
Aimer is a regular -er verb: j'aime, tu aimes, il aime, nous aimons, vous aimez, ils aiment.
Préférer changes é to è in the je, tu, il and ils forms: je préfère, tu préfères, il préfère, nous préférons, vous préférez, ils préfèrent.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order to make a sentence.
exercises.translation: I have a blonde little sister.
exercises.explanation: Petit goes before the noun, but blond goes after it. Both are feminine: petite, blonde.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order to make a sentence.
exercises.explanation: Ne… pas goes around the verb: n'aime pas. Ne becomes n' before a vowel. After aimer, use le, la or les: le sport.

exercises.prompt: Match each masculine job with its feminine form.
exercises.explanation: Many jobs have a feminine form: -eur → -euse (serveuse), -teur → -trice (actrice), add -e (avocate), -ier → -ière (cuisinière), -ien → -ienne (musicienne).

exercises.prompt: Match the French words with their meanings.
exercises.explanation: These words are useful for talking about your family and the people around you.

exercises.source: My brother is tall and blond.
answers: Mon frère est grand et blond.
exercises.explanation: Frère is masculine, so use mon and the masculine adjectives grand and blond (no -e).
Sa matches femme (feminine), not the owner, so it can mean 'his' or 'her'. Canadienne is the feminine of canadien.

exercises.text: Mon père est vendeur et ma mère est avocate.
exercises.translation: My father is a shop assistant and my mother is a lawyer.
exercises.explanation: Listen for the -e of avocate: you hear the t. With a job, French uses no article: il est vendeur.

listening.title: La photo de famille
listening.context: Nadia shows her friend Hugo a family photo on her phone.

lines.speaker: Nadia
lines.fr: Regarde, c'est une photo de ma famille.

lines.speaker: Hugo
lines.fr: Ah, c'est ton père, le grand homme blond ?

lines.speaker: Nadia
lines.fr: Oui. Il a cinquante ans et il est cuisinier.

lines.speaker: Hugo
lines.fr: Et la petite femme brune, c'est ta mère ?

lines.speaker: Nadia
lines.fr: Non, c'est ma tante. Ma mère, c'est la femme avec les lunettes.

listening.translation:
Nadia: Look, this is a photo of my family.
Hugo: Ah, is that your father, the tall blond man?
Nadia: Yes. He is fifty and he is a cook.
Hugo: And the short dark-haired woman, is that your mother?
Nadia: No, that's my aunt. My mother is the woman with the glasses.
Hugo: She's young! Does she work?
Nadia: Yes, she is an English teacher.

questions.question: What is Nadia's father's job?
questions.explanation: Nadia says: « il est cuisinier » (he is a cook). Her mother is the teacher.

questions.question: Who is the short dark-haired woman?
questions.explanation: Nadia says: « Non, c'est ma tante » (No, that's my aunt).

questions.question: How can you recognise Nadia's mother in the photo?
questions.explanation: Nadia says: « Ma mère, c'est la femme avec les lunettes » (the woman with the glasses).

listening.title: Un message de Paul
listening.context: Paul leaves a voicemail for his friend Marie.

lines.speaker: Paul
lines.fr: Samedi, je présente mon ami Kenji à ma famille.

lines.speaker: Paul
lines.fr: Il est japonais, il a vingt-huit ans et il est musicien.

lines.speaker: Paul
lines.fr: Il est très drôle et un peu bavard.

lines.speaker: Paul
lines.fr: Il adore la musique et le cinéma, mais il déteste le football !

lines.speaker: Paul
lines.fr: Tu viens dîner avec nous ? Rappelle-moi. Bisous !

listening.translation:
Paul: Hi Marie, it's Paul!
Paul: On Saturday, I'm introducing my friend Kenji to my family.
Paul: He's Japanese, he's twenty-eight and he's a musician.
Paul: He's very funny and a bit chatty.
Paul: He loves music and the cinema, but he hates football!
Paul: Are you coming to dinner with us? Call me back. Love!

questions.question: What nationality is Kenji?
questions.explanation: Paul says: « Il est japonais » (He is Japanese).

questions.question: What is Kenji's job?
questions.explanation: Paul says: « il est musicien » (he is a musician).

questions.question: What does Kenji NOT like?
questions.explanation: Paul says: « il déteste le football » (he hates football). He loves music and the cinema.

reading.title: Échange de langues
reading.text:
Échange de langues

Bonjour ! Je m'appelle Clara, j'ai vingt-cinq ans et je suis québécoise. J'habite à Montréal avec mon chat, Pixel. Je suis serveuse dans un café. Je suis grande, brune et un peu timide. J'aime la musique, le cinéma et les langues. Je n'aime pas le sport ! Je cherche une amie anglaise ou américaine pour parler anglais et français. Écrivez-moi !
reading.translation:
Language exchange

Hello! My name is Clara, I'm twenty-five and I'm from Quebec. I live in Montreal with my cat, Pixel. I'm a waitress in a café. I'm tall, dark-haired and a bit shy. I like music, the cinema and languages. I don't like sport! I'm looking for an English or American (female) friend to speak English and French. Write to me!

questions.question: Who does Clara live with?
questions.explanation: She writes: « J'habite à Montréal avec mon chat, Pixel. »

questions.question: What is Clara's job?
questions.explanation: She writes: « Je suis serveuse dans un café. » Serveuse is the feminine of serveur.

questions.question: What is Clara looking for?
options: A friend to practise English and French
questions.explanation: She writes: « Je cherche une amie anglaise ou américaine pour parler anglais et français. »

reading.title: La famille d'accueil
reading.text:
Coucou maman !
Ma famille d'accueil à Lyon est super. Monsieur Martin est policier. Il est grand et très gentil. Sa femme, Sophie, est coiffeuse. Elle est petite et rousse. Ils ont deux enfants : Lucas, huit ans, et Emma, cinq ans. Lucas est bavard et Emma est un peu timide. Ils ont aussi un gros chien, Max. Je l'adore !
Bisous,
Aya
reading.translation:
Hi Mum!
My host family in Lyon is great. Mr Martin is a police officer. He is tall and very kind. His wife, Sophie, is a hairdresser. She is short and red-haired. They have two children: Lucas, eight, and Emma, five. Lucas is chatty and Emma is a bit shy. They also have a big dog, Max. I love him!
Love,
Aya

questions.question: What is Sophie's job?
questions.explanation: Aya writes: « Sa femme, Sophie, est coiffeuse. » Mr Martin is the police officer.

questions.question: How many children do the Martins have?
questions.explanation: Aya writes: « Ils ont deux enfants : Lucas… et Emma. » Five is Emma's age.

questions.question: What is Lucas like?
questions.explanation: Aya writes: « Lucas est bavard » (chatty). Emma is the shy one, and Sophie is red-haired.

writing.title: Introduce yourself and a family member
writing.instructions: Write a short message (20–40 words) to Julie, a new French-speaking friend. Give your name, age, nationality and job. Then describe one person in your family and say what they like or don't like.
writing.promptFr: Vous écrivez un petit message à votre nouvelle amie Julie. Présentez-vous (nom, âge, nationalité, profession) et présentez une personne de votre famille. (20 à 40 mots)
writing.modelAnswer: Bonjour Julie ! Je m'appelle Amara, j'ai trente-deux ans et je suis nigériane. Je suis secrétaire. Ma sœur Zainab est grande et très drôle. Elle aime la musique, mais elle n'aime pas le sport. À bientôt ! Amara
checklist: I give my name, my age (j'ai … ans), my nationality and my job.
I describe one family member with two adjectives.
I use mon, ma or mes correctly.
My adjectives agree with the person (grande, canadienne…).
I say what the person likes or doesn't like (aime / n'aime pas).

speaking.title: Introduce yourself
speaking.instructions: The examiner asks you to introduce yourself. Speak for about two minutes: your name, age, nationality, job, what you look like and what you like or don't like.
speaking.promptFr: Bonjour. Présentez-vous, s'il vous plaît : votre nom, votre âge, votre nationalité, votre profession et ce que vous aimez.
speaking.modelAnswer: Bonjour. Je m'appelle Daniel. J'ai trente-quatre ans et je suis ghanéen. J'habite à Toronto avec ma femme. Je suis chauffeur de bus. Je suis grand et brun, et je porte des lunettes. Je suis assez bavard et travailleur. J'aime la musique et le football. J'adore le cinéma aussi. Je n'aime pas le froid ! Je préfère l'été.
tips: Remember: j'ai trente ans, not je suis trente ans.
With a job, don't use un or une: je suis chauffeur, je suis infirmière.
Use aimer, adorer, détester and préférer + le, la or les: j'aime la musique.

speaking.title: Talk about your family
speaking.instructions: The examiner asks you about your family. Speak for about two minutes: who is in your family, their age, their job, what they look like and what they like.
speaking.promptFr: Parlez-moi de votre famille. Vous avez des frères et sœurs ? Comment sont-ils ? Qu'est-ce qu'ils aiment ?
speaking.modelAnswer: Dans ma famille, nous sommes cinq. Mon père s'appelle Ibrahim. Il a soixante ans et il est retraité. Ma mère est professeure. Elle est petite et très gentille. J'ai un frère et une sœur. Mon frère a vingt ans, il est étudiant. Il est grand et un peu paresseux ! Ma sœur est mariée et elle a deux enfants. Elle est avocate. Mes parents adorent leurs petits-enfants. Nous aimons beaucoup les repas en famille.
tips: Use mon for masculine nouns, ma for feminine nouns and mes for plural nouns: mon père, ma mère, mes parents.
Make adjectives agree: mon frère est grand, ma sœur est grande.
Give each person an age, a job and one or two adjectives.

checkpoint.explanation: Amie starts with a vowel, so use mon, not ma. Mes is for plural nouns.
Grand-mère is feminine and starts with a consonant, so it is sa, even for a man. Son is for masculine nouns, ses for plural nouns, leur means 'their'.

checkpoint.promptFr: Je n'aime pas du tout le football. Je ___ le football.
checkpoint.explanation: Ne… pas du tout means 'not at all', so the right verb is détester (to hate). Adorer, préférer and aimer bien are positive.
Amies is feminine and plural: canadien → canadienne → canadiennes.
To ask someone's age, say: Tu as quel âge ? The answer uses avoir: J'ai vingt ans.

checkpoint.prompt: Complete with blond in the correct form.
checkpoint.explanation: Cheveux is masculine plural, so the adjective takes -s: blonds (not blonde).
Adorer is a regular -er verb: j'adore, tu adores, il adore, nous adorons, vous adorez, ils adorent.

checkpoint.prompt: Put the words in order to make a sentence.
checkpoint.translation: He is a young Senegalese teacher.
checkpoint.explanation: Jeune is a short adjective and goes before the noun. Nationalities like sénégalais go after the noun.
Père is masculine, so 'her father' is son père. With a job after être, French uses no article: il est serveur.

checkpoint.source: Leur fille est grande et brune.
answers: Their daughter is tall and dark-haired.
Their daughter is tall with dark hair.
Their daughter is tall and brunette.
Their daughter is tall and has dark hair.
checkpoint.explanation: Leur means 'their' for one thing. Grande and brune are feminine because fille is feminine.
